definition: A technique for improving retrieval by automatically generating additional or reformulated search queries related to the original query.
details: Query expansion can help retrieval systems find relevant documents that use different terminology than the original query, improving recall in both keyword-based and embedding-based search.

explainer.lead: Query expansion improves retrieval by automatically generating additional or reformulated search queries related to the original. It matters because it raises recall, helping systems find relevant documents that use different terminology.

tiers.eli5: If you search for one phrase, the system also tries similar phrases so it doesn't miss pages that word things differently.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add expansion to both keyword-based and embedding-based search to close vocabulary gaps. A pitfall is adding terms so loosely related that precision drops.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition or formula is given; the technique generates additional or reformulated queries related to the original, and its stated benefit is improved recall.

explainer.example: A query is automatically expanded with related reformulations so documents using different wording are still returned.
